Subject: Post-call: Data access controls & support access (FinTrust)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps on the data handling / access controls items we discussed so we’re all aligned: 

Key points from the call:
- FinTrust will be sending low-volume customer PII for enrichment in a private deployment. Primary PII types: name, email, account IDs. No SSNs or full credit card numbers.
- Data residency requirement: US-only (primary region: us-east-1).
- Retention & logging: FinTrust needs 90-day retention for request/response logs and audit logs for 2 years.
- Access controls: RBAC with least-privilege for engineers; break-glass process for production support; full audit trail on any support access.

Action items / owners:
- Alex: confirm final list of PII fields and whether any downstream products will store model outputs (reply by EOD tomorrow).
- Marissa (me): share our RBAC summary, SOC2 snapshot, and break-glass process doc.
- Rishi: prepare a short proposal for support access flow (ticket + time-limited access + recorded session).
- Naomi: I’ll loop in legal if we need to update SLA/data terms in the MSA.

Attachments I’ll share in follow-up: SOC2_summary.pdf, AccessControlOverview.pdf, BreakGlass_Process.docx.

Proposed next meeting: 30 minutes next week to review our proposed support-access flow and finalize mutual action plan. Can we aim for Tue 7/21 at 11am ET?

Thanks —

Marissa Cole

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Confirming PII: name, work email, FinTrust customer ID. No SSNs or payment data will be sent.
- Residency: must remain in US regions only; primary preference is us-east-1 but us-west-2 is acceptable for DR if encrypted at rest and in transit.
- Retention: we can accept 90-day request/response logs; audit logs retention needs to be 24 months. Will your system support immutable audit logs export?

For support access, our security team needs:
- Role-based access separation (we prefer explicit role names and permissions matrix).
- Break-glass: time-limited elevated access with mandatory ticket + approval from our security on-call, and session recording.
- Evidence of prior incidents: can you provide an example of how a support-access event is logged (redacted) and what the notification flow looks like?

Attached is our completed security questionnaire — it has a couple of specific asks on key management and network allowlists.

Alex
Director, Infrastructure Security
FinTrust
[attachment: FinTrust_security_questionnaire_answers.pdf]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintrust.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-16T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Data access controls & support access (FinTrust)

Alex — thanks, this is helpful. Quick answers below and attached docs for details.

- Residency & encryption: we support region pinning per account. All data in transit is TLS1.3; at-rest encryption uses customer-managed KMS (optional). We can commit to primary in us-east-1 and DR in us-west-2 with encryption. See SOC2_summary.pdf for controls and KMS details.

- Audit logs & retention: yes — we provide immutable audit logs via append-only exports to your S3 bucket (or we can retain on our side for the agreed 24 months). Export example (redacted) attached.

- RBAC model (summary):
  * admin: full account config + billing (restricted to 2-3 FTEs)
  * eng: deploy + view invocation metadata (no access to raw PII by default)
  * analyst: aggregated metrics and reports only
  * support: time-limited elevated role with explicit justifications logged

- Break-glass & support access flow (high-level):
  1) Support ticket created in ServiceNow/Jira with FinTrust approver.
  2) Approval triggers a time-limited ephemeral credential (AWS STS-style) scoped to the session.
  3) Session is recorded; all commands and KV cache access are logged and pushed to your audit S3.
  4) Automated alert to FinTrust security and named contacts.

Attached: AccessControlOverview.pdf (matrix) and BreakGlass_Process.docx (step-by-step). Also sharing a short example of an audit log export as AccessControlMatrix.xlsx.

Next steps:
- Alex: confirm whether you want exports to your S3 or retention on our side.
- Rishi: I’ve flagged the support flow questions for you to draft proposed SLAs for time-limited access and notification windows.

Happy to jump on the Tue 7/21 slot if that works — I’ll send a calendar invite once we lock it.

Best,

Marissa
